verdict.rationale: Omarchy ships OpenCode and Claude Code as default agent harnesses. It invites you to set up a default agent on first boot, and integrates that agent into the OS: crash notifications send the agent to diagnose, and bundled skills let it build apps, plugins and themes. However, the assistant is a third-party agent you sign into rather than a first-party built-in AI, and its delegation scope is only shown through vendor claims. Missing for 10: a first-party native assistant (not bundled third-party harnesses needing external sign-in), documented depth and limits of system-wide task delegation, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the agent integrations.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: On first boot, Omarchy invites you to set up a default agent. Pick your favorite, sign in, and put it to work on your computer.
When an app crashes, click the notification to send your agent on the case. It can examine the crash dump, diagnose what went wrong, and help report the bug.
Omarchy ships with [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/) and [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) as the default agent harnesses for programmers.
Omarchy ships with skills to help your agent make apps, plugins, and themes.
